evidence: Receiving online DO at 52h = 10.33 mg/L; recent 4h window min 10.33, mean 10.95 mg/L — large margin over 2 mg/L limit
Receiving product assays: 0.022 g/L @12h, 0.026 @24h, 1.117 @36h, 2.912 @48h — exponential production phase matching source-1/2/3 patterns (2.98–3.06 g/L @47.8h)
physical_forward_model keep: product_mass_kg=576.3, post_decision min DO=7.35 mg/L, below_limit_h=0, post_decision_feasible=true; all 5 sensitivity members feasible (min DO range 6.22–8.48)
Source batches ran to 96h with DO staying 8–14 mg/L throughout, indicating sustained aeration capacity under identical load
args.rationale: Observations show a normal, healthy receiving fermentation: DO at 52 h is ~10.3 mg/L (well above the 2 mg/L hard limit, no downward excursion; lowest recent value still 10.3 mg/L) and product is on a strong growth trajectory (2.91 g/L at 48 h, matching source-batch behavior). The source-calibrated forward model for KEEP predicts zero hours below the DO limit, minimum post-decision DO ~7.35 mg/L, terminal product mass ~576 kg, and all 5 sensitivity members feasible (min DO 6.2–8.5 mg/L). Feed-reduction actions would needlessly reduce product mass and stop would zero counted production, with no oxygen-constraint benefit since no deficit is predicted. Among supported feasible plans, KEEP retains maximal product mass.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and may mismatch the hidden receiving realization; however, the DO margin is large (current 10.3 vs limit 2.0 mg/L, predicted minimum 7.3 mg/L, worst sensitivity member 6.2 mg/L), so forecast error of several mg/L would still leave the constraint satisfied. Product trajectory may differ from source, but this affects yield, not the hard oxygen constraint. No evidence of contamination or abnormal DO dips exists in the public observations.
